usageNotes: Use this as the second step in the node shell VNC flow: first call the node's 'vncshell' endpoint to obtain a port (5900–5999) and a short-lived vncticket, then use those values here to upgrade the HTTP connection to a WebSocket carrying VNC traffic. The vncticket expires quickly, so the WebSocket upgrade must happen promptly after the vncshell call. The caller must hold Sys.Console on /nodes/{node}.

examples.summary: Open VNC WebSocket to node shell using port and ticket from a prior vncshell call

tips: This endpoint is intended to be called as an HTTP Upgrade (WebSocket handshake), not a plain REST GET — standard REST clients will not establish a useful connection.
The port value must exactly match what was returned by the preceding vncshell call; ports are single-use and bound to the ticket.
vnctickets are time-limited (typically ~2 minutes); do not cache them for later reuse.
API tokens are allowed (allowtoken: true), but the vncticket itself is the second authentication factor required by the permission check.
